prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1490; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the policyholder's representative after a low-speed head-on collision; the claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy period.

Entry 3: Obtained the statement of the other driver, who confirms the accident happened as described. Two independent witnesses and the scene photographs are consistent with the same sequence of events.

Entry 4: Reviewed the vehicle damage, which is mostly in line with the impact described. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records.

Entry 5: Claimant reports neck and back strain. The injury pattern appears to match the kind and force of a crash of this type. No prior injury to the same body areas is known from records available so far.

Entry 6: Still unclear from the statements and photos exactly where in the vehicle the claimant was seated at impact, so this has been put to counsel for clarification.

Entry 7: Claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far, including the initial report, the recorded statement, and the follow-up call.

Entry 8: Treatment has followed a usual course, with care tapering as the claimant's symptoms improved. Medical records received through counsel are being reviewed against the treatment timeline.

Entry 9: File reviewed and set for continued handling. Next step is to request the final treatment summary and reassess the bodily injury evaluation once it is received.
